title: SACL V1 control-plane and agent-execution governance

owns: Deterministic validation and authorization boundaries for SACL execution packages.
Traceability between requirements, contracts, implementation, tests, and CI evidence.
Role boundaries and fail-closed escalation for delegated agent work.
non_goals: This specification does not authorize SACL runtime activation or real agent execution.
This specification does not authorize production access, remote production execution, deployment, or merge.
This specification does not replace the frozen Decision Baseline or existing architecture invariants.

functional_contracts.requirement: MUST validate every specification document against the closed JSON Schema before it can be accepted by CI.
MUST resolve every parent specification and reject missing parents, duplicate identifiers, and inheritance cycles.
MUST reject a child specification that removes or changes a parent invariant or weakens inherited security restrictions.
MUST produce a non-zero process exit code when any specification or inheritance check fails.
MUST preserve human approval as the authority for architecture changes, irreversible actions, and operational activation.

invariants.statement: MUST preserve the precedence order in DECISION_BASELINE.md and contracts/architecture-invariants.json.
MUST keep hard local deny above project policy, package requests, and approval grants.
MUST treat execution packages and agent-produced artifacts as untrusted input until validated.
MUST keep implementation_authorized false unless the human principal explicitly changes the governing authorization.
MUST keep main pushes, merges, deployments, production mutations, and real-host certification behind separate explicit human authorization.
MUST retain immutable traceability from specification identifiers to acceptance scenarios and CI evidence.

must_not: Agent-generated package content MUST NOT grant itself executable authority.
A valid approval MUST NOT override a hard-deny policy.
Secrets, OAuth tokens, signing keys, or production credentials MUST NOT be written to Git or agent prompts.
CI mocks MUST NOT be represented as proof of real-host compatibility or production readiness.
An agent MUST NOT modify a frozen contract without an approved, versioned architecture decision.

forbidden_dependencies: Unapproved runtime dependencies or network services.
Direct production database or cloud mutations from CI.
Unverified Antigravity lifecycle hooks or tool matchers treated as security boundaries.

may: Define business outcomes and acceptance criteria in measurable terms.
must_not: MUST NOT select implementation frameworks or silently alter frozen technical contracts.

may: Define module boundaries, dependency direction, public interfaces, and versioned architecture decisions.
must_not: MUST NOT override explicit human decisions or proven behavior without an approved decision record.

may: Own DDL, migrations, relational constraints, indexes, and persistence invariants.
must_not: MUST NOT modify production data or weaken schema constraints without explicit approval.

may: Implement code within the assigned target paths and approved interfaces.
must_not: MUST NOT change public signatures, frozen schemas, or dependencies outside the assigned contract.

may: Create deterministic unit, integration, regression, and property-based tests from approved contracts.
must_not: MUST NOT change production code to make tests pass or weaken acceptance criteria.

may: Audit code, dependencies, permissions, and policy bypass paths; block unsafe changes.
must_not: MUST NOT approve its own remediation or suppress findings without recorded rationale.

may: Issue a machine-verifiable acceptance or rejection verdict against the specification and test evidence.
must_not: MUST NOT infer acceptance from narrative claims, green badges, or unverified artifacts.

acceptance_scenarios.given: No valid execution package is queued and no approved work is pending.
acceptance_scenarios.when: The persistent supervisor evaluates the next scheduling cycle.
acceptance_scenarios.then: The supervisor remains idle and does not launch an LLM worker.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A package requests an operation denied by hard local policy.
acceptance_scenarios.when: The policy lattice evaluates the effective permissions.
acceptance_scenarios.then: The request is denied even if the package or approval requests that operation.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A candidate implementation changes a frozen invariant or omits its required test evidence.
acceptance_scenarios.when: The specification and CI gates evaluate the candidate.
acceptance_scenarios.then: The candidate is rejected and no downstream integration or deployment is triggered.

acceptance_scenarios.given: An agent exhausts its configured retry budget or encounters a specification conflict.
acceptance_scenarios.when: The orchestration workflow reaches its escalation boundary.
acceptance_scenarios.then: The work is blocked with a structured diagnostic and awaits human arbitration.
